title: Treadmill-based task for assessing spatial memory in head-fixed mice
author: Jordan, McDermott, et al.

steps.title: Set up data acquisition computer
steps.instruction: Install MATLAB version 2020a or newer on a PC equipped with a National Instruments PCIe‑6323 data acquisition card; place the scripts RunTreadmill.m and OpenTreadmillFile.m in a folder that is on the MATLAB path. (Alternative DAQ systems such as Raspberry Pi‑based setups can be used.)

steps.title: Insert axle rods and encoder
steps.instruction: Insert axle rods into the custom ball‑bearing plates. Before insertion, gently remove the optical rotary encoder wheel and encoder from its plastic housing, attach the encoder to the custom plate with matching screw holes, then insert the axle (with encoder attached) into the bearings.

steps.title: Assemble treadmill wheel frame
steps.instruction: Mount 1‑inch aluminum rails vertically on an air table to form the frame. Space the two rails for each wheel to match the distance between the ball‑bearing plates, and position the two wheels approximately 50 cm apart with the platform centered between them.

steps.title: Build platform and attach RFID scanner
steps.instruction: Affix the RFID scanner to the bottom of the platform with heavy‑duty electrical tape directly under the mouse path. Solder the scanner wires and isolate each with heat‑shrink tubing to prevent short‑circuits from vibration. Set the platform height about 0.5 cm lower than the top of the wheels.

steps.title: Mount head‑plate brackets
steps.instruction: Attach the head plate to its brackets, then secure the brackets to a pair of rails so the head plate sits roughly 2.5 cm above the platform. Monitor mouse behavior for belt‑texture issues and adjust belt quality if mice have trouble pulling the belt or remain stationary.

steps.title: Construct treadmill belt with tactile cues
steps.instruction: Cut velvet fabric into 7.5 cm‑wide strips; join four 45 cm strips to make a 180 cm belt (staple or sew, but do not close into a ring until the belt is wrapped around the wheels). Add tactile cues (e.g., sandpaper circles of different grit or hot‑glue stripes) as needed. Attach five RFID tags (four for zone transitions, one for the reward site) to the underside with duct tape. Wrap the belt around the wheels and platform, then join the ends (staple or sew). Belt material may differ from the key‑resources table but must be light enough for the mouse to pull and must not slip on the foam wheels.

steps.title: Assemble reward port and lick counter connection
steps.instruction: Solder a wire to a metal gavage needle and plug this wire into the lick counter. Assemble the reward port using the gavage needle, tubing, and a 10 mL syringe placed in the clamp of a micro‑infusion pump; program the pump for 10 µL water pulses. Position the reward port with a flexible‑arm clamp near the mouse’s snout during trials and move it away when attaching or removing the mouse.

steps.title: Connect Arduino controllers and cables
steps.instruction: Wire the rotary encoder and RFID reader to Arduino microcontrollers and connect all wires and BNC cables according to the instructions in the lab’s GitHub repository (https://github.com/GoncalvesLab/HeadFixedTreadmill).

steps.title: Run initial treadmill test
steps.instruction: Execute a short (~1 minute) test session using RunTreadmill.m; verify that water rewards are delivered. Then run OpenTreadmillFile.m and follow the top‑script instructions to confirm that data from all treadmill components are being recorded correctly. Perform this test at the start of each training day or immediately after changing belts or reward locations.

steps.title: Set up TTL synchronization for neural recordings
steps.instruction: Generate a transistor‑transistor‑logic (TTL) signal from the recording apparatus and connect its wire to an input channel of the NI data acquisition hardware at the beginning and end of each recording session (or per video frame) to synchronize behavioral and neural data.

steps.title: Assemble grounding pin for lick counter
steps.instruction: Clamp a gold pin in a helping‑hand alligator; insert a tungsten wire into the shallow hole of the pin’s flat end, solder, then trim the wire to ~1 mm from the pin. Solder a female connector to a longer wire that will link the implanted pin to the lick counter, providing the ground needed for lick detection.

steps.title: Prepare sterile surgery area
steps.instruction: Set up a sterile field with a scalpel, forceps, and a dental curing light (Optibond and Flow‑It Accelerated Light Cure composite adhesives) for implantation of the headbar and grounding pin.

steps.title: Compute lick maps for analysis
steps.instruction: Using the custom analysis software, divide the 180 cm belt into 3 cm bins, calculate the fraction of total licks occurring in each bin, and generate a normalized lick‑rate map to visualize spatial licking behavior.

steps.title: Conduct probe trial without reward
steps.instruction: Turn off the reward pump, then run a session as usual. Expect an overall drop in lick rate while licking remains concentrated near the former reward zone. Optionally, make reward delivery contingent on detection of licking within the reward location.
